advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider distinguishing 'excluded legacy dict' from 'typed mutation unexpectedly missing target' rather than silently dropping both in the typed_mutations filter.
evidence: run_differs.py:284: `typed_mutations = [m for m in ctx.mutations if getattr(m, "target", None) is not None]`

Mutation.__post_init__ enforces `if not isinstance(self.target, str) or not self.target: raise ValueError` (mutation.py:56-57), so a well-formed typed Mutation always has a truthy target — the silent drop only bites for malformed/foreign objects
The exclusion has no counter/diagnostic distinguishing 'skipped a legacy dict' from 'a typed item unexpectedly lacked target'
advisory.finding: The typed_mutations filter `[m for m in ctx.mutations if getattr(m, 'target', None) is not None]` silently drops any mutation lacking a truthy .target. This is intended to exclude legacy plain-dict mutations, but the miss path is silent: a malformed typed Mutation (or any object) missing .target would also be dropped from the plan with no signal, indistinguishable from a correctly-excluded legacy dict.
